title: Expose the keryx harness over the Agent Client Protocol so any ACP client can drive it

AC1.note: src/acp/protocol.ts pins ACP_PROTOCOL_VERSION=1 and negotiateProtocolVersion; a newer version is answered with the latest keryx supports, a malformed or out-of-range one with a JSON-RPC error; stdout purity asserted over a real pipe (src/acp/conformance.process.test.ts)

AC2.note: session/new binds the session to resolveProjectRoot(cwd); session/prompt runs a real harness turn and the conformance test compares the agent_message_chunk updates to the fixture's text_deltas one for one, so a buffered end-of-turn flush fails it

AC3.note: a gated call is announced then asked through session/request_permission; only an explicit allow runs it, and an unoffered option, cancel, malformed answer, error or silence all deny; a policy that denies outright never reaches the client (src/acp/permission.test.ts and the process tests)

AC4.note: session/cancel aborts the turn the way a local stop does, settles a pending ask as a denial and answers cancelled, with no further session/update for that turn (src/acp/cancel-list-load.process.test.ts)

AC5.note: session/list and session/load speak for the project's own durable sessions; a keryx shell session is listed and loaded with its history replayed in the spec's shape, and an unreadable transcript is answered with a named error instead of an empty replay

AC6.note: reads route through fs/read_text_file when advertised and fall back to the local tool when not; the capability matrix test proves no fs/* call without the capability and no terminal/* in any configuration; the write and shell limits are recorded in the code with their reasons (AC amended during the flow with its reason)

AC7.note: the wire types, framing, method partition and capabilities live in src/acp/protocol.ts, pinned by a test that fails if a protocol name or version leaks anywhere else (src/acp/protocol.test.ts)

AC8.note: src/acp/conformance.process.test.ts drives one subprocess through the whole surface over a real stdio pipe with a fixture provider and asserts the order of the traffic; every wait is on a wire event, not a timer

AC9.note: README documents keryx acp and the docs CLI reference carries the per-method table, what a client must advertise, what keryx does when a capability is absent, the session-busy refusal and the transcript error; acp added to the top-level command table

AC10.note: CI 18/18 green on PR 646 at head 6355b5c1 (merged 2026-09-22T20:37Z as 57c2a37b); keryx health run PASS, no gate conditions triggered

AC1 as frozen contradicted the ACP v1 spec: a client asking for a newer protocol version MUST be answered with the latest version the agent supports, not refused. Refusal stays for a malformed or out-of-range version. Found by the T5 surface pinning against the published schema; no criterion had been confirmed yet.

AC6 as frozen demanded that writes route through fs/write_text_file. apply_patch applies a multi-file diff atomically through git; the ACP write method writes one file's whole content with no diff semantics and no cross-file atomicity, so routing it would be a redesign, not a capability branch. AC6 now states what the design guarantees — reads route when advertised, writes and shell stay local with the reason recorded, and no absent capability is ever called — and the routing work is left to a follow-up flow.
